chroot_dir.description: Directory to use as the root of the chroot environment (if chroot is enabled).

debug.description: Enable verbose debugging output (to syslog).

idle_timeout.description: Seconds of inactivity after which the connection is closed.

max_connections.description: Maximum number of simultaneous connections. 0 means unlimited.

pam_service_name.description: Name of the PAM service configuration file (without .conf), used for authentication and password change.

password_change_command.description: Optional command to run instead of using PAM for password changes (e.g., for legacy compatibility).

pid_file.description: Full path to write the process PID file. Leave empty or unset to disable PID file creation.

port.description: TCP port to listen on (standard POP password change port is 106). Set to 0 to disable direct listening (e.g., for inetd/xinetd).

syslog_facility.description: Syslog facility to use for logging (e.g., 'daemon', 'local0', 'local1').

chroot_dir.description: Root directory for the chroot jail (must be populated)

chroot_enabled.description: Enable chroot jail for enhanced security

daemon_group.description: System group the POP3 daemon runs as (for privilege dropping)

daemon_user.description: System user the POP3 daemon runs as (for privilege dropping)

debug.description: Enable debug mode (logs extensive detail)

idle_timeout.description: Seconds of inactivity before disconnecting a client

lockout_duration.description: Seconds to lock out an account after max failed attempts

log_failed.description: Log failed login attempts (useful for security auditing)

maildir_format.description: Use Maildir format (one file per message) instead of mbox (one file per mailbox)

max_connections.description: Maximum number of simultaneous client connections

max_failed_attempts.description: Maximum failed login attempts before locking the account

sasl_db_path.description: Path to SASL password database file

sasl_enabled.description: Enable SASL authentication (e.g., for PLAIN/LOGIN over TLS)

spooldir.description: Directory where user mailboxes (mbox or maildir) are stored

tls_certfile.description: Path to TLS certificate file (PEM format)

tls_enabled.description: Enable TLS encryption for secure connections

tls_keyfile.description: Path to TLS private key file (PEM format)

top_enabled.description: Enable the POP3 TOP command (allows partial message retrieval)

uidl_enabled.description: Enable the POP3 UIDL command (unique message identifiers)

block_host.description: Automatically block detected attackers (by adding to /etc/hosts.deny or firewall rules).

block_time.description: Duration (seconds) to block a host before unblocking (set 0 for permanent block).

detection_window.description: Time window (seconds) during which connection attempts are counted for scan detection.

ignore_icmp.description: Disable detection for ICMP traffic (set to true to ignore ICMP packets).

ignore_udp.description: Disable detection for UDP traffic (set to true to ignore UDP packets).

kill_cmd.description: Custom command to run when blocking a host (e.g., for alerting or logging).

max_connections.description: Maximum connections allowed per host per detection window (0 = unlimited).

scan_mode.description: Which traffic to monitor: 'tcp' (TCP SYN, FIN, etc.), 'udp' (UDP), or 'both'.

stealth_scan_threshold.description: Number of connection attempts per host within the detection window to trigger an alert.

strict_tcp_scan.description: Enable detection of non-standard TCP scans (XMAS, NULL, FIN, SYN-ACK, etc.).

strict_udp_scan.description: Enable detection of suspicious UDP patterns (e.g., fragmented packets, unusual ports).

tcp_mode.description: TCP scanning mode: 'tcp' (standard), 'stcp' (stealth), 'atcp' (aggressive stealth), or empty to disable.

udp_mode.description: UDP scanning mode: 'udp', 'sudp', 'audp', or empty to disable.

autovacuum_analyze_scale_factor.description: Fraction of table size added to analyze threshold.

autovacuum_analyze_threshold.description: Minimum tuple updates before analyze is triggered.

autovacuum_max_workers.description: Maximum number of autovacuum worker processes.

autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor.description: Fraction of table size added to vacuum threshold.

autovacuum_vacuum_threshold.description: Minimum tuple updates before vacuum is triggered.

checkpoint_completion_target.description: Fraction of checkpoint interval over which WAL writes are spread (0.0–1.0). Higher = smoother I/O.

data_directory.description: Absolute path to the database cluster data directory.

hba_file.description: Absolute path to the client authentication config file (pg_hba.conf).

ident_file.description: Absolute path to the user name mapping file (pg_ident.conf).

listen_addresses.description: Which IP addresses/ hostnames the server listens on. Use '*' for all interfaces.

log_directory.description: Directory for log files (relative to data_directory or absolute path).

log_filename.description: Pattern for log filenames (supports strftime placeholders).

log_line_prefix.description: Prefix for each log line. Format codes: %m=timestamp, %p=pid, %u=user, %d=db, etc.

log_min_duration_statement.description: Log statements slower than this (ms). -1 disables. Use 1000 to log queries >1s.

log_rotation_age.description: Max age of a log file before rotation (e.g., '1d', '24h').

log_rotation_size.description: Max size of a log file (in bytes) before rotation. 0 = unlimited.

logging_collector.description: Enable logging to files (instead of stderr).

maintenance_work_mem.description: Maximum memory for maintenance operations (VACUUM, CREATE INDEX, etc.).

max_connections.description: Maximum number of concurrent connections allowed.

max_wal_size.description: Maximum size of WAL files before a forced checkpoint.

min_wal_size.description: Minimum size of WAL files to retain after cleanup.

port.description: The TCP port the PostgreSQL server listens on.

shared_buffers.description: Amount of memory dedicated to caching data (e.g., '256MB', '1GB'). Recommended ~25% of total RAM for dedicated DB servers.

wal_buffers.description: Shared memory for WAL writes. Set to -1 for automatic tuning.

wal_level.description: WAL level: 'minimal' (no replicas), 'replica' (basic replication), or 'logical' (logical replication & logical decoding).

work_mem.description: Memory per operation (e.g., sort, hash) before spilling to disk. Higher values speed complex queries but multiply with connections.

db_engine.description: Database engine: 'sqlite', 'mysql', or 'postgres'. SQLite is standard for most Postfix setups.

db_path.description: Path to the database file used for storing greylisting records. SQLite is used by default.

greylist_max_age.description: Maximum seconds after which greylisting records expire (i.e., after how long a sender must re-greylist).

greylist_seconds.description: Minimum seconds to wait before accepting mail from a new sender. Typical value: 300 (5 minutes).

listen_address.description: IP address on which postgrey listens for incoming SMTP connections from Postfix. Usually localhost.

listen_port.description: TCP port number for postgrey to bind to. Default Postfix port for greylisting is 10023.

log_file.description: Path to log file when syslog is disabled. Ignored if syslog is enabled.

loglevel.description: Verbosity level: 0 (quiet), 1 (normal), 2 (verbose). Set higher if troubleshooting.

postgrey_text.description: Custom greylist rejection message text. Used only if set (non-empty).

run_as_group.description: Optional system group to run the daemon under. If empty, uses the primary group of `run_as_user`.

run_as_user.description: System user account to run the postgrey daemon under. Should have read/write access to the database file.

syslog.description: If true, log to system syslog. If false, log to file instead.

whitelist_clients_delay.description: Time (in seconds) before greylisting is skipped for whitelisted clients. Set to 0 to skip greylisting entirely for them.

whitelist_postfix_smtpd.description: If true, skip greylisting for mail submitted via postfix local smtpd.

whitelist_recipients_delay.description: Time (in seconds) before greylisting is skipped for whitelisted recipients. Set to 0 to disable greylisting for them.

chroot_dir.description: Chroot directory for security hardening. Standard is '/var/lib/postsrsd'.

debug.description: Enable verbose logging (true) or quiet operation (false). Not directly configurable here; use extra_daemon_options instead.

listen_addr.description: IP address to bind the postsrsd socket to. Use '127.0.0.1' for local Postfix; '0.0.0.0' only if remote.

max_connections.description: Maximum concurrent connections allowed. Not configurable in this init script; limited by kernel/daemon defaults.

srs_domain.description: Domain used for SRS rewriting (e.g., the domain of your mail server). Must be a valid, verified domain.

srs_forward_port.description: TCP port on which postsrsd listens for Postfix lookup queries. Standard is 10001.

srs_hashlength.description: Length of the hash suffix appended to rewritten addresses. Standard is 4.

srs_hashmin.description: Minimum hash length for validation. Usually same as hashlength.

srs_reverse_port.description: TCP port used for reverse SRS lookups (bounce handling). Usually 10002.

srs_secret.description: Path to file containing the secret key for signing/verifying SRS addresses. Must be ≥16 chars, randomly generated, and kept secret.

srs_separator.description: Separator character used in SRS addresses. Standard is '==' (two equals signs).

auto_detect.description: Enable automatic detection and monitoring of newly connected battery devices

critical_threshold.description: Battery percentage at or below which a 'critical' alert is triggered

log_level.description: Verbosity of logging; choose from debug, info, warning, error

notification_script.description: Path to script invoked on battery status changes (receives device name, status, and % capacity)

notification_timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the notification script before timing out

pid_file.description: Path to store the daemon's PID file

smtp_password.description: SMTP password (leave blank if no authentication)

smtp_server.description: SMTP server hostname (used only if email alerts enabled)

smtp_use_tls.description: Use TLS encryption for SMTP connection

smtp_user.description: SMTP username (leave blank for unauthenticated SMTP)

tick_interval.description: Number of seconds between battery status polls

warning_threshold.description: Battery percentage at or below which a 'warning' alert is triggered

log_ppp_connect_errors_path.description: Path to the ppp connection errors log file.

log_rotate_count.description: Number of rotated log files to keep.

history_dir.description: Directory where preload stores access history (patterns of file reads) for learning.

max_processes.description: Maximum number of processes the daemon will track simultaneously. Larger values increase memory usage.

passive.description: Whether to reactively read ahead *only* when a process actually opens a file.

preload_iosched.description: I/O scheduling class to use for preload (e.g., '--iosched idle').

proactive.description: Whether to proactively load files for frequently-used processes *before* they are opened (improves responsiveness, but may increase disk usage).

profile_dir.description: Directory where preload stores readahead profiles for known files and applications.

readahead_pages.description: Maximum number of pages to read ahead per I/O request. Set to 0 to use the kernel's default value.

scan_interval.description: How often (in seconds) the daemon scans the system for new processes and updates its database.

global_listen_addr.description: IP address the proxy listens on. Use '127.0.0.1' for localhost-only.

global_listen_port.description: Port the proxy listens on for incoming SMTP (typically 25, 587, or 465).

global_log_file.description: Path to the main log file. Leave empty to log to stdout/stderr.

global_log_level.description: Logging verbosity: debug, info, notice, warning, error, critical.

global_pid_file.description: Path to the PID file for the ProxSMTP daemon.

global_run_dir.description: Directory where runtime files (e.g., PID files) are stored.

tls_ca_file.description: Optional path to CA bundle for client certificate verification.

tls_cert_path.description: Path to the server TLS certificate file (PEM format). Required if TLS is enabled.

tls_enabled.description: Enable TLS for inbound connections (STARTTLS or implicit TLS depending on port).

tls_key_path.description: Path to the server TLS private key file (PEM format). Required if TLS is enabled.

allow_multiple_sources.description: Allow multiple timing sources. Useful for redundancy or grandmaster failover.

announce_interval.description: Interval between Announce messages (seconds). Typical: 1 or 2.

clock_identity_source.description: How clock identity is generated: 'hw' (MAC-based, recommended) or 'sw' (random).

delay_asymmetry.description: One-way path asymmetry (nanoseconds). Used only with peer-to-peer delay mechanism.

delay_req_interval.description: Minimum interval between Delay_Req messages (seconds). Set to 1 or 2.

domain_number.description: PTP domain number (0–65535). All devices in the same time domain must match.

hw_timestamping.description: Enable hardware timestamping for sub-microsecond precision (recommended).

initial_frequency.description: Initial frequency correction (parts-per-billion) applied at startup.

log_level.description: Logging verbosity (0=fatal, 7=debug). Set to 2 or 3 for production; 4+ for debugging.

log_sync_messages.description: Log every SYNC message for deep diagnostics (can be very verbose).

primary_domain.description: Fallback domain number when domain mismatch occurs.

ptp_device.description: Explicit PTP device (e.g., '/dev/ptp0'). Leave empty to auto-detect.

slave_only.description: If true, this device behaves only as a slave (ordinary clock). Set false for boundary clocks.

sync_interval.description: Interval between Sync messages (seconds). Use -1 for 'as fast as hardware allows'.

transport_mode.description: Transport mode. Use 'udp' for most deployments; 'ieee_1588' for legacy L2-only setups.

PTPD_OPTS.description: Additional command-line options to pass to ptpd (e.g., --interface eth0 --domain 0).

enabled.description: Start the PTP daemon on service startup.

enforce_src.description: If true, only accept ICMP packets from IPs listed in allowed_src_nets.

listen_interface.description: Network interface to listen on. Use 'auto' to let ptunnel auto-detect.

log_file.description: Path to log file. Leave empty to log only to stdout/stderr.

max_idle_time.description: Maximum inactivity (in seconds) before a tunnel is forcibly closed.

max_tunnels.description: Maximum number of concurrent tunnels (TCP connections) allowed.

password.description: Password for securing the tunnel. Must be identical on both client and server.

ping_delay.description: Delay (in milliseconds) between consecutive ping packets. Lower = more aggressive, higher = more reliable through firewalls.

ping_dest_port.description: ICMP destination port used in the ICMP tunnel (must match between client and server). 0 = echo request.

ping_size.description: Size (in bytes) of ICMP payload. Larger sizes may improve throughput but increase fragmentation.

ping_ttl.description: Time-to-live (TTL) value for outgoing ICMP packets. 0 = use system default.

remote_dst.description: Target remote IP address for the ICMP tunnel (required on the receiving end).

run_daemon.description: Set to "true" to enable the ptunnel daemon (must be set to 'true' to start the service).

tunnel_timeout.description: Timeout (in seconds) after which an idle tunnel is closed.

verbose.description: Enable verbose logging? If true, logs at normal level. Use 0 or 1 explicitly for fine control.

cni_conf_dir.description: Path to CNI network configuration directory.

debug_level.description: Log level for containerd (debug, info, warn, error, etc.).

default_runtime_name.description: Default container runtime to use for containers (e.g., 'runc', 'kata-runtime').

devmapper_pool_name.description: Device mapper pool name (if using devmapper snapshotter).

enable_cri.description: Enable the CRI plugin to support Kubernetes container runtime API.

grpc_address.description: Unix socket path for containerd gRPC API.

grpc_max_recv_message_size.description: Maximum gRPC receive message size in bytes.

grpc_max_send_message_size.description: Maximum gRPC send message size in bytes.

image_deletion.description: Enable automatic deletion of unused images (recommended in production).

image_pull_timeout.description: Timeout for image pull operations in seconds (0 = unlimited).

max_container_log_size.description: Maximum size (in bytes) of container stdout/stderr logs.

metrics_interval.description: Interval (seconds) between metric exports (set to 0 to disable).

no_pivot.description: Disable pivot root (not recommended for production — useful only in constrained environments).

overlayfs_native_diff.description: Use native diff algorithm for overlayfs snapshots (slower but accurate; fallback if 'diff' fails).

pprof_enabled.description: Enable pprof CPU/memory profiling endpoint (disabled by default).

privileged_without_host_devices.description: Grant privileges to containers without exposing host devices (Kubernetes-specific).

root_dir.description: Root directory for persistent containerd data (snapshots, image layers).

sandbox_image.description: Image used for Kubernetes sandbox (pause) containers.

snapshotter.description: Default snapshotter used for container filesystem layers (e.g., 'overlayfs', 'btrfs', 'devmapper').

state_dir.description: Directory for containerd runtime state (sockets, PID files, etc.).

delivery.ehlo.description: Name to use in EHLO/LHLO commands.

delivery.lmtp_socket.description: Path to LMTP Unix socket (only used if method=lmtp).

delivery.recipient.description: Message recipient. If empty, defaults to the username associated with the effective user ID.

headers.add_date.description: Ensure each message has a Date: header (add if missing).

headers.add_received.description: Add a 'Received:' header showing this forwarder's action.

headers.replace_from.description: If non-empty, overwrite the From: header with this email address.

imap.auth.description: Space-separated list of preferred authentication mechanisms (PLAIN, LOGIN, etc.).

imap.compress.description: Use the IMAP COMPRESS extension if advertised by the server.

imap.fetch_batch_size.description: Number of messages to fetch per IMAP batch to avoid timeouts.

imap.host.description: IMAP server hostname or IP address. Can optionally be enclosed in square brackets to force IP literal interpretation.

imap.mailbox.description: IMAP mailbox name to pull messages from (UTF-7 encoded and unquoted).

imap.password.description: IMAP login password (store securely in production — e.g., via secrets manager or file permissions).

imap.port.description: IMAP server port (143 for non-SSL, 993 for SSL).

imap.ssl.description: Enable SSL/TLS for the IMAP connection (equivalent to type=imaps).

imap.username.description: IMAP login username (often full email address).

limits.max_concurrent_jobs.description: Maximum parallel message deliveries at once.

limits.max_message_size.description: Largest message size (in bytes) to process. 0 = unlimited.

limits.rate_limit_per_minute.description: Maximum messages delivered per minute. 0 = unlimited.

logging.level.description: Minimum log level: debug, info, warn, error.

logging.log_file.description: Path to file where logs are written (empty = no file logging).

main.statefile.description: State file to track mailbox UIDVALIDITY and UIDNEXT values. Relative paths start from $XDG_DATA_HOME/pullimap or ~/.local/share/pullimap.

purge.retention_days.description: Retention period in days (≥24h accuracy due to IMAP SEARCH). 0 = delete immediately after delivery.

tls.SSL_CAfile.description: File containing trusted certificates for server verification.

tls.SSL_CApath.description: Directory to use for server certificate verification (must be in hash format).

tls.SSL_fingerprint.description: Space-separated list of acceptable fingerprints for server certificate SPKI (e.g., sha256$<hex>).

tls.SSL_hostname.description: Name to use for TLS SNI (Server Name Indication). Empty string disables SNI.

tls.SSL_protocol_max.description: Maximum SSL/TLS protocol version (e.g., TLSv1.2, TLSv1.3).

tls.SSL_protocol_min.description: Minimum SSL/TLS protocol version (e.g., TLSv1.2, TLSv1.3).

tls.SSL_verify.description: Whether to verify the server certificate chain and match its SAN/CN against host.

tls.ca_file.description: Path to CA certificate bundle for verifying the SMTP/LMTP server certificate.

tls.enable.description: Enable TLS for outgoing SMTP/LMTP connections.

compile_timeout.description: Maximum time (seconds) to wait for a compile job before terminating it; empty or 0 means no timeout

compression.description: Compression level for network traffic (0=off, 1=fast, 9=best); empty or 0 disables compression

enable_daemon.description: Whether to enable the daemon mode to accept remote compilation requests

log_file.description: Path to log file; use 'stdout' or 'stderr' to log to console

log_level.description: Verbosity of logging: 0 (error), 1 (warn), 2 (info), 3 (debug)

max_connections.description: Maximum number of simultaneous client connections and concurrent compilation jobs

port.description: TCP port on which the distcc daemon listens for incoming connections

tempdir.description: Directory used to store temporary files during compilation

user.description: System user to drop privileges to after starting; leave empty to disable privilege dropping

host.description: IP address to bind to (e.g., '0.0.0.0', '127.0.0.1', '::'). Must be provided if `bind_tcp` is used.

port.description: Port number to listen on. Must be provided if `bind_tcp` is used.

db_host.description: Hostname or IP address of the PostgreSQL server.

db_name.description: Name of the PostgreSQL database to use.

db_password.description: Password for the database user. Leave empty if using peer auth or SSL certs.

db_ssl.description: Whether to use SSL when connecting to PostgreSQL.

db_ssl_ca_cert.description: Path to CA certificate used to verify the PostgreSQL server.

db_ssl_cert.description: Path to client certificate for PostgreSQL SSL authentication.

db_ssl_key.description: Path to client private key for PostgreSQL SSL authentication.

db_type.description: Database backend. PuppetDB supports only PostgreSQL.

db_user.description: Database user account PuppetDB will connect as.

ha_enabled.description: Enable high-availability mode (requires external database HA & load balancer).

http_host.description: Interface to bind the HTTP endpoint to. Use '0.0.0.0' for all interfaces (not recommended in production without TLS).

https_host.description: Interface to bind the HTTPS endpoint to.

https_ssl_ca_cert.description: Path to CA cert used to verify client certificates (optional).

https_ssl_cert.description: Path to SSL certificate for HTTPS.

https_ssl_key.description: Path to private key for HTTPS. Must be world-readable if owned by root.

java_args.description: Java arguments passed to PuppetDB JVM (e.g., memory limits, GC options, JMX settings).

log_level.description: Verbosity of PuppetDB logging. Valid values: debug, info, warn, error, fatal.

max_connection_pool_size.description: Maximum number of database connections in the pool.

node_purge_ttl.description: Time after which inactive nodes are purged from the database.

query_max_queue_size.description: Maximum number of queued queries before rejecting.

query_workers.description: Number of threads used to process queries concurrently.

request_timeout.description: Maximum time to wait for a request (e.g., '30s', '5m').

api_v1_services_enabled.description: Route agent service requests through the v1 API (legacy); leave disabled for Puppet v7+

ca_enabled.description: Enable the Certificate Authority (CA) service; disable only for ca-bundle-only or proxy deployments

ca_max_serial_numbers.description: Maximum number of certificates to track in memory (increase for large infrastructures)

ca_name.description: Human-readable CA identifier (e.g., 'Puppet CA: prod-puppet-01'); leave empty for auto-generated

jvm_java_home.description: Path to Java 11+ runtime (JRE or JDK); Puppet Server requires Java 11–17

log_level.description: Root logging level: 'trace', 'debug', 'info', 'warn', 'error', or 'fatal'

puppet_server_hostname.description: Primary hostname for this Puppet Server (used as fallback for cert-hostname and CA name)

webserver_cert_hostname.description: Hostname used in SSL certificates for the web server (overrides cert-hostname in auth.conf); leave empty to use `puppet_server_hostname`

webserver_enabled.description: Enable the Puppet Server HTTP web interface (required for admin tools and status endpoints)

client_character_set.description: Default character set for MySQL client connections.

client_port.description: Default port used by MySQL client tools.

mysqld_bind_address.description: IP address MySQL listens on. Use 0.0.0.0 to listen on all interfaces (ensure firewall is configured).

mysqld_binlog_enabled.description: Enable binary logging (required for replication and point-in-time recovery).

mysqld_binlog_format.description: Binary log format: STATEMENT, ROW, or MIXED. ROW is safest for replication.

mysqld_binlog_path.description: Base name/path for binary log files (without extension).

mysqld_character_set_server.description: Default character set for new databases and tables.

mysqld_collation_server.description: Default collation for the server (must match the character set).

mysqld_datadir.description: Directory where MySQL stores table data and system databases.

mysqld_expire_logs_days.description: Number of days after which binary logs are automatically purged.

mysqld_innodb_buffer_pool_size.description: Size of the buffer pool used to cache InnoDB data and indexes. For dedicated DB servers, set to ~70–80% of RAM.

mysqld_innodb_flush_method.description: Method used to flush data to InnoDB data files and logs. Common: fsync, O_DIRECT.

mysqld_innodb_log_file_size.description: Size of each InnoDB log file in the log group. Larger values improve performance but increase crash recovery time.

mysqld_long_query_time.description: Threshold in seconds for queries to be logged as slow.

mysqld_max_allowed_packet.description: Maximum size of a single packet or any generated/intermediate string. Must be a number + unit (e.g., 64M, 256M).

mysqld_max_connections.description: Maximum number of simultaneous client connections allowed.

mysqld_port.description: TCP port for MySQL server connections.

mysqld_query_cache_size.description: Total size of the query cache (deprecated in MySQL 8.0+; leave empty to omit.)

mysqld_query_cache_type.description: Query cache behavior: 0=OFF, 1=ON, 2=DEMAND. (Deprecated in MySQL 8.0+; leave empty to omit.)

mysqld_server_id.description: Unique server ID (1–4294967295). Required for replication; must be unique per server in the topology.

mysqld_slow_query_log_enabled.description: Enable slow query logging (for performance analysis).

mysqld_slow_query_log_file.description: Path to the slow query log file.

system_max_files.description: Maximum number of system journal files to keep (0 = unlimited)

write_user_session_messages.description: Log user session manager messages to the journal

handle_hibernate_key.description: Action to take when hibernate button is pressed

handle_lid_switch.description: Action to take when laptop lid is closed. Accepts: ignore, poweroff, reboot, halt, kexec, suspend, hibernate, hybrid-sleep, suspend-hybrid, shutdown

handle_lid_switch_docked.description: Action to take when lid is closed while docked/externally powered (overrides HandleLidSwitch). In shipped default, HandleLidSwitchExternalPower defaults to 'suspend'; HandleLidSwitchDocked defaults to 'ignore'. Here we follow shipped default comments.

handle_power_key.description: Action to take when power button is pressed. Accepts: ignore, poweroff, reboot, halt, kexec, suspend, hibernate, hybrid-sleep, suspend-hybrid, shutdown

handle_suspend_key.description: Action to take when suspend button is pressed

kill_user_processes.description: Whether to kill user processes when they log out. Accepts: yes, no, on-last-log

n_auto_vts.description: Number of virtual terminals (VTs) to manage automatically

remove_ipc.description: Whether to remove user IPC objects (shared memory, etc.) on logout. Accepts: yes, no, on-last-log

cache_size.description: Maximum number of DNS entries to cache (positive integer, 0 disables caching).

caching.description: Enable caching of DNS responses (recommended for performance).

dns_max_retries.description: Maximum number of retries for a DNS query before giving up.

dns_stub_listener_port.description: Port on which systemd-resolved listens for local DNS queries (0 disables stub listener).

dns_timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for a DNS query response before retrying.

dnssec.description: Enable DNSSEC validation of responses. Note: requires DNSSEC-capable upstream servers.

dnssec_cache_max_size.description: Maximum number of DNSSEC-validated resource records to cache (0 = no separate limit).

negative_ttl.description: Time in seconds to cache negative (NXDOMAIN/NOERROR) responses.

preserve_dns.description: Keep the DNS stub listener socket in place across daemon restarts (prevents client reconnects).

read_etc_hosts.description: Whether to resolve hostnames via /etc/hosts before querying DNS.

resolve_unicast_reverse_lookups.description: Enable reverse lookups (PTR) via mDNS (may conflict with nss-mymachines).

tcp_dns_queries.description: Send DNS queries over TCP instead of UDP (useful for bypassing broken UDP infrastructure).

use_llmnr.description: Enable or disable Link-Local Multicast Name Resolution (LLMNR).

use_mdns.description: Enable or disable Multicast DNS (mDNS) for resolving .local domains.

max_steps_threshold_sec.description: Maximum clock offset (in seconds) that triggers a step instead of gradual slew. Offsets beyond this cause an immediate jump.

poll_interval_max_sec.description: Maximum interval (in seconds) between polls. Higher values reduce network usage but slow detection of clock drift.

poll_interval_min_sec.description: Minimum interval (in seconds) between successive polls to the same server. Lower values increase responsiveness but traffic.

preserve_system_clock.description: If enabled, systemd will save and restore system time across reboots to reduce drift. Safe and recommended for most systems.

root_distance_max_sec.description: Maximum allowed root distance (round-trip delay to authoritative time source) in seconds. Servers exceeding this are rejected.

server_poll_interval_dampening.description: Poll interval growth factor during instability (e.g., 2 = exponential backoff). Higher values reduce oscillation but slow recovery.

step_backward.description: Whether to allow stepping the clock backward (e.g., after network partition recovery). Set to `true` only if your services tolerate backward time jumps.

state_path.description: Directory where kactivitymanagerd stores its persistent state; must be writable by the user.

xdg_runtime_dir.description: XDG Base Directory for user runtime files; %U will be expanded by systemd to the user ID.

auto_unmount_timeout.description: Seconds of inactivity before auto-unmounting a device. Set to 0 to disable auto-unmount.

automount.description: Whether to automatically mount removable media (e.g., USB sticks, SD cards) when inserted.

automount_internal_drives.description: Whether to automatically mount internal drives (e.g., internal SATA/PCIe SSDs/HDDs) — use with caution.

enable_lvm2.description: Enable udisks2 support for LVM2 logical volumes (requires lvm2 tools on system).

enable_mdraid.description: Enable udisks2 support for MD RAID arrays (requires mdadm tools on system).

ignore_encrypted.description: If true, skip auto-mounting of encrypted devices (e.g., LUKS). Manual unlocking is required.

log_dir.description: Directory for log files generated by udisks2.

log_level.description: Logging verbosity: 0=ERROR, 1=WARN (recommended for production), 2=INFO, 3=DEBUG.

maximum_uid.description: Maximum allowed UID for auto-mounted volumes (must be ≥ minimum_uid).

minimum_uid.description: Minimum allowed UID for auto-mounted volumes (prevents accidental root ownership conflicts).

ntfs_mount_readonly.description: Mount NTFS volumes as read-only by default if ntfs-3g (full NTFS write support) is not available.

polling_enabled.description: Enable polling (instead of relying solely on udev events) for removable media insertion/removal.

state_dir.description: Directory for runtime state (e.g., device cache, lock files). Should be a tmpfs location for speed.

user.description: User account to own auto-mounted volumes. Often set to a regular user for desktop systems.

batch.description: Run in non-interactive mode — abort on any prompt requiring user input. Useful for cron jobs.

copier.description: Conflict resolution strategy. 'newer' (default): copy file from side with newer timestamp. 'error' stops on conflicts.

delete.description: Whether to delete files that exist on only one side. Options: 'yes', 'no', 'nonroot' (default for bidirectional — deletes only from non-root roots, i.e., from the secondary side).

fastcheck.description: Use fast MD5-based checksums for large files to reduce network transfer during comparison.

follow.description: Whether to follow symbolic links. Valid: 'true', 'false', 'both'.

log.description: Enable logging of synchronization actions to console.

logfile.description: Path to a log file. If empty, no file logging is done.

perms.description: Preserve file permissions and ownership (requires proper filesystem support and privileges).

port.description: SSH port to use when connecting to remote hosts. Set to 0 to use default SSH port (22).

prefer.description: Which side to prefer when a conflict occurs (newer file wins). Other options: older, error, never.

retry.description: Number of times to retry connection on network failure before aborting.

sshcmd.description: Command to use for SSH connections. You can specify custom options (e.g., 'ssh -p 2222 -i /id_ed25519').

times.description: Preserve modification times (timestamps) of files during sync.

verbose.description: Verbosity level: 0 (quiet) to 4 (detailed debug). Higher values show more info about each step.

add_to_known_hosts.description: Whether to automatically add IPA-managed hosts to ~/.ssh/known_hosts.

allow_trusted_domains.description: Whether to allow authentication from trusted Active Directory domains (if configured in IPA).

base_dn.description: Base DN for LDAP searches (e.g., 'dc=example,dc=com'). Auto-discovered if omitted.

cache_credentials.description: Whether to cache user credentials for offline authentication.

configure_sshd.description: Whether to configure the SSH daemon to use SSSD for IPA authentication.

create_homedir.description: Whether to automatically create a home directory for IPA users on first login.

dns_discovery.description: Whether to use DNS SRV records to discover IPA domain controllers.

dns_forwarder.description: DNS forwarder IP for dynamic DNS updates (e.g., '8.8.8.8'). Leave blank to disable.

dns_lookup_max_depth.description: Maximum recursion depth when using DNS to discover IPA servers. Set to 0 to disable DNS SRV lookups.

dns_lookup_realm.description: Whether to use DNS to discover IPA realm (Kerberos realm discovery via SRV records).

enumerate.description: Whether to enumerate all IPA users and groups (may impact performance on large directories).

krb5_conf.description: Path to the Kerberos configuration file. Usually /etc/krb5.conf.

krb5_realm.description: Explicit Kerberos realm name if different from the IPA realm. Defaults to 'realm'.

ldap_uri.description: Custom LDAP URI for IPA server (e.g., 'ldap://ipa.example.com'). Auto-discovered if omitted.

min_id.description: Minimum UID/GID to consider valid (prevents conflicts with local accounts).

prompt_password.description: Custom text to prepend before password prompts (leave blank for default).

realm.description: The name of the IPA domain (e.g., 'example.com'). Must match the IPA server domain.

server.description: Hostname or IP of the primary IPA server (e.g., 'ipa.example.com').

ssh_keys.description: Whether to enable retrieval and use of SSH public keys for IPA users.

update_ssh_client_config.description: Whether to automatically update ~/.ssh/config with IPA host keys on login.

use_otp.description: Whether to enable one-time password (OTP) authentication for IPA users.

use_sssd.description: Whether to configure the system to use SSSD for user/group lookups and authentication.

bind.description: Source address to bind when connecting (e.g., 0.0.0.0 or ::)

cert.description: Path to TLS client certificate file

USERGROUPS.description: If yes, create a private group for each new non-system user.

host-name.description: Set the host name avahi-daemon tries to register on the LAN.

host-name-from-machine-id.description: Use machine-id as name on the LAN.

objects-per-client-max.description: Maximum number of objects per D-Bus client.

publish-aaaa-on-ipv4.description: Publish IPv6 AAAA records via IPv4 when IPv4 is enabled.

publish-resolv-conf-dns-servers.description: Publish DNS servers from /etc/resolv.conf in addition to publish-dns-servers.

publish-workstation.description: Register a _workstation._tcp service for LAN discovery.

ratelimit-interval-usec.description: Per-interface packet rate-limiting interval in microseconds.

reflect-filters.description: Comma-separated list of allowed service names to reflect.

reflect-ipv.description: Forward mDNS traffic between IPv4 and IPv6 when reflector is enabled.

rlimit-as.description: Value in bytes for RLIMIT_AS (virtual memory limit).

rlimit-core.description: Value in bytes for RLIMIT_CORE (core file size limit).

rlimit-data.description: Value in bytes for RLIMIT_DATA (data segment size limit).

use-iff-running.description: Monitor IFF_RUNNING flag to detect network link status.

use-ipv4.description: If set to no, avahi-daemon will not use IPv4 sockets.

use-ipv6.description: If set to no, avahi-daemon will not use IPv6 sockets.

username.description: One or more whitespace-separated usernames, or the wildcard '*'.

challenge_password_otp.description: Whether the SCEP challenge password is treated as a one-time password.

enroll_ttls.description: List of times (in seconds) before certificate expiration to attempt renewal.

notification_destination.description: Destination for notifications: syslog priority.facility, email address, or command.

notify_ttls.description: List of times (in seconds) before certificate expiration to issue warnings.

populate_unique_id.description: Whether to populate subjectUniqueID and issuerUniqueID in self-signed certificates.

symmetric_cipher.description: Symmetric cipher used to encrypt private keys in PEM format.

validity_period.description: Validity period for self-signed certificates (format: 1y, 2w, etc.).

authselectmode.description: Determines the default selection policy for authenticated and unauthenticated sources.

clockprecision.description: Specifies the precision of the system clock in seconds.

combinelimit.description: Limits sources included in the combining algorithm by synchronization distance. 0 disables combining.

dscp.description: Sets the DSCP value for transmitted NTP packets.

initstepslew.description: Corrects system clock by stepping or slewing at boot based on a threshold and list of servers. (Deprecated)

manual.description: Enables runtime support for the settime command in chronyc.

maxdistance.description: Maximum acceptable root distance for source synchronization.

maxjitter.description: Maximum allowed jitter for sources before rejection by the source selection algorithm.

ntstrustedcerts.description: Specifies files or directories containing trusted certificates for NTS.

peer.description: Specifies a symmetric NTP peer association.

pool.description: Specifies a pool of NTP servers as a time source.

refclock.description: Specifies a hardware reference clock as a time source.

refresh.description: Interval in seconds between refreshing IP addresses of NTP sources. 0 disables periodic refresh.

reselectdist.description: Fixed distance added to non-selected sources to avoid frequent reselection.

server.description: Specifies an NTP server as a time source.

stratumweight.description: Distance added per stratum during source selection.

.pragma.description: Set parsing behavior flags (e.g., abspath, dollarid, includedir).

ssl_conf.description: Name of the section containing SSL/TLS configuration sections.

AllowResharingRemoteCUPSPrinters.description: Whether remote CUPS print queues are re-shared to the local network.

AutoClustering.description: Whether to automatically cluster remote CUPS queues with same name.

AutoShutdownTimeout.description: Seconds of inactivity before auto-shutdown occurs (0 = immediate).

BrowseDeny.description: Denies printers from specified hosts or networks (IP or CIDR notation or 'All').

BrowseFilter.description: Filters remote printers by properties (e.g., name, host, TXT record fields); supports NOT and EXACT options.

BrowseLocalProtocols.description: Protocols used to advertise local shared printers on the network.

BrowseOrder.description: Determines order of applying BrowseAllow and BrowseDeny rules.

BrowsePoll.description: Polls specific servers (host:port or just host) for available printers every 60 seconds.

BrowseProtocols.description: Protocols used for both finding remote and advertising local printers.

BrowseRemoteProtocols.description: Protocols used to find remote shared printers.

BrowseTimeout.description: Maximum time (in seconds) allowed per browsing operation (e.g., adding/removing a queue).

CacheDir.description: Directory where cups-browsed saves information about generated print queues on shutdown.

Cluster.description: Manually define printer clusters for load balancing.

CreateRemoteCUPSPrinterQueues.description: Whether to create local queues for shared remote CUPS queues.

CreateRemoteRawPrinterQueues.description: Whether to create local queues for remote raw CUPS queues.

DNSSDBasedDeviceURIs.description: Whether to use DNS-SD-service-name-based device URIs (for DNS-SD-discovered printers only).

DebugLogFileSize.description: Maximum size (in KB) of debug log files; 0 = unlimited.

DebugLogging.description: Controls debug logging destination: file, stderr, or none.

CacheDir.description: Sets the directory for persistent temporary (cache) files.

SyncOnClose.description: Controls whether fsync() is called after writing config/state files.

User.description: Sets the user used when running external programs.

bip.description: Bridge IP address and CIDR (e.g., 172.17.0.1/16) for the default docker0 bridge network.

containerd.description: Path to the containerd socket (typically auto-detected).

data_root.description: Root directory for Docker persistent data (images, volumes, etc.).

debug.description: Enable verbose debug logging for troubleshooting.

default_gateway_v6.description: IPv6 default gateway for containers on the default bridge.

exec_root.description: Root directory for exec-related temporary files.

fixed_cidr_v6.description: IPv6 subnet for container allocation when IPv6 is enabled.

log_driver.description: Default logging driver for containers (e.g., json-file, syslog, journald).

max_concurrent_downloads.description: Maximum number of concurrent downloads per image pull (higher = faster pulls but more network use).

max_concurrent_updates.description: Maximum number of concurrent image update operations (e.g., for Swarm updates).

max_concurrent_uploads.description: Maximum number of concurrent uploads per image push.

max_containers.description: Maximum number of containers allowed to run simultaneously (0 = unlimited).

mtu.description: Maximum Transmission Unit for the default bridge network.

pidfile.description: Path to the Docker daemon PID file.

storage_driver.description: Storage driver to use for images and containers (e.g., overlay2, vfs, zfs).

userland_proxy.description: Whether to use Docker's userland proxy for port mapping (required for some edge cases).

bwlimit.description: Set I/O bandwidth limits for various operations (in KiB/s).

consent-text.description: Consent text displayed before logging in.

description.description: Datacenter description shown in the web interface.

email_from.description: Email address to send notifications from.

fencing.description: Set the fencing mode of the HA cluster.

http_proxy.description: External HTTP proxy used for downloads.

keyboard.description: Default keyboard layout for VNC server.

mac_prefix.description: Prefix for auto-generated MAC addresses of virtual guests.

max_workers.description: Maximal number of workers per node for actions like stopall VMs.

migration_unsecure.description: Deprecated: disable SSH tunnel encryption for migration.

next-id.description: Control the range for VMID auto-selection pool.

registered-tags.description: List of tags requiring Sys.Modify on / to set/delete.

BACKUP_SUFFIX.description: Compression algorithm suffix for the home directory backup (e.g., .gz, .bz2).

BACKUP_TO.description: Directory where backup files are stored when BACKUP is enabled.

EXCLUDE_FSTYPES.description: Regex of filesystem types to skip when searching for user files to delete.

NO_DEL_PATHS.description: List of regex patterns; files matching any pattern are not deleted.

ONLY_IF_EMPTY.description: If enabled, group is removed only if it has no members.

REMOVE_ALL_FILES.description: Removes all files owned by the user anywhere in the system.

REMOVE_HOME.description: Removes the user's home directory and mail spool.

exclude.description: Specify trailing directories to exclude during module search.

external.description: Specify external directories to be searched for modules, with kernel version regex or wildcard.

override.description: Override which version of a specific module is used, given module name, kernel version, and subdirectory.

search.description: Specify the order in which module subdirectories are processed by depmod.

allowinterfaces.description: Limit discovered interfaces to those matching pattern(s).

arping.description: Perform ARP probing for address(es) before DHCP.

authprotocol.description: Authenticate DHCP messages using specified protocol.

bootp.description: Operate as a BOOTP client only.

controlgroup.description: Set group ownership of control socket.

debug.description: Echo debug messages to stderr and syslog.

destination.description: Set listed DHCP options to interface destination address.

duid.description: Specify or override DHCP Unique Identifier type.

embed.description: Embed sub-option inside custom defined option.

encap.description: Encapsulate sub-options inside custom defined option.

env.description: Push variable to environment for hooks.

fallback.description: Fall back to specified profile if DHCP fails.

hostname_short.description: Send short hostname instead of FQDN.

ia_na.description: Request DHCPv6 Normal Address for iaid.

ia_pd.description: Request DHCPv6 Prefix Delegation and assign prefixes to interfaces.

ia_ta.description: Request DHCPv6 Temporary Address for iaid.

inform.description: Send DHCP INFORM with optional address/cidr/broadcast.

interface.description: Set interface scope for subsequent options.

ipv6ra_autoconf.description: Enable SLAAC address generation per RA auto flag.

ipv6ra_fork.description: Always fork on receiving IPv6 RA.

leasetime.description: Request lease time in seconds (-1 for infinite).

link_rcvbuf.description: Override kernel link receive buffer size.

msuserclass.description: Add Microsoft user class string (single only).

mudurl.description: Specify MUD URL for upstream access control.

noalias.description: Remove pre-existing IPv4 addresses on new address.

noauthrequired.description: Accept unauthenticated messages even if auth requested.

nodhcp.description: Skip DHCP and listening to DHCP messages.

nodhcp6.description: Skip DHCPv6 and listening to DHCPv6 messages.

noup.description: Do not bring interface up in manager mode.

persistent.description: Retain configuration on exit (do not deconfigure).

profile.description: Set profile scope for subsequent options.

randomise_hwaddr.description: Randomize hardware address on link up or loss.

reboot.description: Timeout before moving to DISCOVER on reboot.

request.description: Request specific IP address in DHCP DISCOVER.

require.description: Require option(s) to be present, ignore otherwise.

ssid.description: Set wireless SSID scope for subsequent options.

static.description: Configure static value (e.g., ip_address, router, etc.).

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (0 = wait forever).

userclass.description: Add user class string(s) to DHCPv4 message.

vendclass.description: Add DHCPv6 Vendor Identifying Vendor Class.

waitip.description: Wait for specified IP protocol(s) before forking.

xidhwaddr.description: Use last 4 bytes of hardware address as DHCP xid.

addn_hosts.description: Path to an additional hosts file (e.g., '/etc/dnsmasq/hosts') to append to the in-memory host table. Maps to the `--addn-hosts` option.

cache_size.description: Size of the DNS cache (number of records). Set to 0 to disable caching. Maps to `--cache-size` (man page: default 150, max 10000). Type should be integer, not number.

dhcp_enabled.description: Enable or disable DHCP server functionality.

dhcp_gateway.description: Gateway IP to assign to DHCP clients (DHCP option 3). If omitted, no gateway is set. Maps to `--dhcp-option=option:router`.

dhcp_port.description: Server port for DHCP. Maps to `--dhcp-port` (man page: changes ports from default 67/68 to specified value). Default is 67.

dns_port.description: Port on which dnsmasq listens for DNS queries. Maps to `--port`. Setting to 0 disables DNS.

domain_name.description: Local domain name (e.g., 'lan') to append to unqualified hostnames. If not set, domain-less queries won’t be expanded.

expand_hosts.description: Whether to automatically append the local-domain to unqualified names in /etc/hosts and static-hosts entries. Maps to the `--expand-hosts` option.

ignore_hosts.description: Whether to ignore entries in /etc/hosts for DHCP (only use static_hosts). Prevents accidental overrides. Note: There is no direct `ignore_hosts` equivalent in dnsmasq. The closest is using `--dhcp-hostfile=/dev/null` to read DHCP host info from /dev/null instead of /etc/hosts. This schema maps to that behavior.

log_file.description: Log file path. Use '-' to log to stderr/syslog, or '/var/log/dnsmasq.log' for a file. Maps to `--log-facility`. If the value contains a '/', it's treated as a filename.

log_level.description: Log verbosity level (0 = quiet, 1+ = enable query logging). When >= 1, enables `log-queries`. Maps to the presence of `--log-queries` rather than a numeric value directly. Note: dnsmasq's `log-queries` doesn't take a numeric argument; setting the directive enables logging. There is no `log-level` option in dnsmasq.

DEFAULT.description: Value to assign to the variable if no value is already set.

OVERRIDE.description: Value to assign if an existing value should override the DEFAULT.

VARIABLE.description: Name of the environment variable to configure.

admin_group.description: Group whose members are treated like root (subject to even_deny_root and root_unlock_time).

audit.description: Log user name to system log if user not found.

deny.description: Deny access after n consecutive failures within the interval.

dir.description: Directory where user failure record files are kept.

even_deny_root.description: Allow root account to be locked like regular users.

local_users_only.description: Track failed attempts only for local users in /etc/passwd.

no_log_info.description: Suppress logging of informative messages via syslog.

nodelay.description: Skip enforcing delay after authentication failures.

root_unlock_time.default: defaults to unlock_time if not set
root_unlock_time.description: Seconds after lockout before root access is re-enabled (implies even_deny_root).

silent.description: Suppress informative messages to the user.

unlock_time.description: Seconds after lockout before access is automatically re-enabled.

as-path.description: Replacement path used in cached information for <remap-dir>.

binding.description: Binding strength for values added or modified by <edit>.

ignore-blanks.description: When true, ignore blanks in string comparisons for 'eq' and 'not_eq'.

ignore_missing.description: Whether to suppress warnings when an <include> target file or directory is missing.

mode.description: Determines how <edit> modifies the target property.

prefix.description: Path prefix for directory paths in <dir>, <cachedir>, and <include> elements.

qual.description: Controls whether <test> matches any or all values of the property.

salt.description: Salt value used to determine cache filename, for distinguishing identical paths with different content.

target.description: Determines whether the <match> element applies to the original pattern, matched font, or font during scanning.

type.description: Value type used in <patelt>, expression, or comparison elements (internal to parser, not user-configurable directive).

label.description: Adds entries to the label table used in RFC 3484 sorting; each entry specifies a netmask and precedence value.

precedence.description: Adds entries to the precedence table used in RFC 3484 sorting; each entry specifies a netmask and precedence value.

reload.description: Controls whether to reread the configuration file on each getaddrinfo() call.

wal_level.description: WAL level: 'minimal' (no replicas), 'replica' (basic replication), or 'logical' (logical replication & logical decoding).

aliases.description: optional space- or tab-delimited aliases for the protocol

number.description: the official protocol number for use in the IP header

protocol.description: the native name for the protocol (e.g., ip, tcp, udp)

debug.description: Turns on debugging via syslog(3).

enforce_for_root.description: If this option is set, the check is enforced for root, too.

file.description: Store password history in file /path/filename rather than the default location.

remember.description: The last N passwords for each user are saved.

retry.description: Prompt user at most N times before returning with error.

badwords.description: Space-separated list of prohibited words (beyond dictionary check).

dcredit.description: Maximum credit for digits; if negative, minimum required digits.

dictcheck.description: Check password against dictionary (cracklib); 0 disables check.

difok.description: Number of characters in the new password that must not be present in the old password.

enforce_for_root.description: Apply checks even for root user (yes) or allow root to override (no).

enforcing.description: Reject password on failure (1) or just warn (0); affects pam_pwquality only.

gecoscheck.description: Check if GECOS words (≥4 chars) appear in password; 0 disables check.

lcredit.description: Maximum credit for lowercase letters; if negative, minimum required lowercase letters.

maxsequence.description: Maximum allowed length of monotonic character sequences; 0 disables check.

minclass.description: Minimum number of required character classes (digits, uppercase, lowercase, others).

minlen.description: Minimum acceptable size for the new password (plus one if credits are not disabled).

ocredit.description: Maximum credit for other characters; if negative, minimum required other characters.

retry.description: Maximum number of password prompts before error.

ucredit.description: Maximum credit for uppercase letters; if negative, minimum required uppercase letters.

usercheck.description: Check if username appears in password (min 3-char usernames skipped); 0 disables check.

usersubstr.description: Check for substrings of length ≥ N in password; requires >3.

auto_bridge.description: Automatically create a bridge interface (e.g., virbr0) for NAT networking.

auto_bridge_name.description: Name of the auto-created bridge interface.

auto_memory_tune.description: Enable automatic memory tuning (e.g., hugepages, NUMA placement). Disable for manual control.

default_cpu_model.description: Default CPU model exposed to guests. 'host-passthrough' exposes host features for best performance.

default_dns.description: DNS server used by guest VMs when using user-mode networking.

default_tpm_backend.description: Default TPM backend: 'emulator' uses software TPM, 'passthrough' uses host hardware TPM.

default_video_model.description: Default graphics adapter for VMs. 'qxl' works well with SPICE; 'virtio' for minimal overhead.

emulator.description: Override the default QEMU emulator binary (e.g., 'qemu-system-aarch64'). Leave empty to auto-detect.

group.description: Group ownership for QEMU processes.

hotplug.description: Enable hotplug for disks and NICs. Required for dynamic resource scaling.

io_threads.description: Number of dedicated I/O worker threads. Higher values may improve I/O throughput on multi-core systems.

live_snapshot.description: Enable taking snapshots of running VMs without downtime.

log_file.description: Path to the log file when log_output is set to 'file'.

log_level.description: Logging verbosity: 0=none, 1=error, 2=info, 3=debug. Use 2 for general troubleshooting.

log_output.description: Where to send QEMU logs: 'file', 'syslog', or 'stderr'.

max_vcpus.description: Maximum virtual CPUs allowed per guest. Adjust based on host CPU topology.

memory_backing.description: Memory backing mode for VMs. 'hugepages' improves performance on large guests.

migration.description: Enable or disable VM live migration capability.

migration_address.description: IP address for incoming migration traffic. Use '0.0.0.0' to listen on all interfaces.

migration_port.description: Base port for migration traffic. Migrating VMs use sequential ports in the range.

migration_ports.description: Number of ports (starting from migration_port) reserved for concurrent migrations.

monitor_protocol.description: Protocol used for QEMU monitor communication. 'json' is recommended for automation.

monitor_stdin.description: Enable QEMU monitor on stdin. Disable to prevent accidental console access.

netns.description: Run QEMU processes in a private network namespace. Isolates network stack for security.

numa_auto_allocation.description: Automatically allocate guest memory to NUMA nodes. Disable for manual NUMA pinning.

sandbox.description: Enable seccomp sandboxing to restrict system calls. Keep enabled for security.

seccomp_sandbox.description: Enable seccomp filters to restrict system calls. Keep enabled unless troubleshooting.

shared_block.description: Allow multiple VMs to share the same block device. Requires external coordination (e.g., GFS2).

spice_listen.description: IP address on which SPICE servers listen. Similar to VNC, restrict to '127.0.0.1' for security.

spice_tls.description: Enable TLS encryption for SPICE remote desktop connections.

tee.description: Enable support for Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) devices (e.g., Intel TDX).

tpm.description: Enable TPM (Trusted Platform Module) support in guests.

uefi_firmware.description: Enable UEFI firmware support (OVMF/AAVMF). Required for UEFI guests.

use_cgroups.description: Use cgroups v2 for CPU and memory resource control. Required for advanced QoS.

user.description: User account under which QEMU processes run. Use 'qemu' or a dedicated non-root user for security.

vhost_user.description: Enable vhost-user (userspace virtio backend) support for high-performance networking.

vnc_listen.description: IP address on which VNC servers listen. '127.0.0.1' restricts to local host; '0.0.0.0' allows all interfaces.

vnc_tls.description: Enable TLS encryption for VNC remote desktop connections. Required for secure access.

aof_load_truncated.description: Load AOF even if it appears truncated (prevents startup failure on partial writes).

aof_use_rdb_preamble.description: Prefix AOF with RDB snapshot for faster load (recommended).

appendfsync.description: Sync policy: always, everysec, no. Trade-off between durability & performance.

appendonly.description: Enable AOF persistence (recommended over RDB alone for durability).

auto_aof_rewrite_min_size.description: Minimum AOF size required to trigger rewrite (e.g., '64mb', '128mb').

auto_aof_rewrite_percentage.description: Trigger AOF rewrite when size grows by this % over last rewrite.

bind.description: IP address(es) Redis will bind to (space-separated for multiple). Use '0.0.0.0' to bind to all interfaces (⚠️ insecure unless firewall-protection is applied).
